indicators.note: rolled suggests turning something over, so the letters of 'a pastry's' are read backwards

parts.note: tarts are pastries; the possessive gives the plural-looking TARTS

explanation.surface: A baker describes the flaky layers of a rolled-out pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' turns A TARTS end to end. 'Pastry's layers' looks like one phrase, but the definition is 'layers' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, as of rock or of society; a direct synonym.

indicators.note: about means the word for reading wraps around a letter

parts.note: study means reading, as in reading for a degree
R stands for arithmetic, one of the three Rs of basic schooling

explanation.surface: Is studying about sums a tough business?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside STUDY. The three Rs are reading, writing and 'rithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means robust and tough, a sense of hard.

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: keeping means the word for mum holds a letter inside it

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A note says Mum is holding up well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not a mother but the adjective 'quiet'; 'keeping' puts I inside SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient means tough and able to recover, close to strong.

parts.note: though means however, nevertheless
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Even when stressed, someone might try meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective for a stressed person; it is the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Meditation is an example of thought, hence the 'perhaps'.

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
trapped means stuck, unable to get out

explanation.surface: A card player stuck holding spades ends up penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being strapped for cash is an idiom for being short of money, i.e. broke.

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: tolled means rang, as a bell does

explanation.surface: Someone apparently phoned and admitted everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' gives the sound of TOLLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have told is to have revealed or admitted something, as in told all.

clue.text: Worker from start is a newbie

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tradesman who has been a novice right from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker or craftsman.

parts.note: monarchs here are the butterflies, so future ones are at the chrysalis stage

explanation.surface: Princes and princesses in line to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Monarchs suggest royal heirs, but a monarch is also a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects in the chrysalis stage become butterflies such as the monarch.

clue.text: Forlorn sweetheart almost alone in rendezvous

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the word for a rendezvous

parts.note: a date is a romantic rendezvous
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for alone is dropped

parts.note: sole means only, alone

explanation.surface: A lonely lover, nearly alone, waits miserably at a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' reads as a lover but means the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter; 'almost' drops a final letter, and 'in' places both inside the meeting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means wretched and abandoned, a synonym of forlorn.

parts.note: UPS is the American parcel-delivery firm
hot means keen, as in hot on an idea

explanation.surface: A delivery firm is eager to settle a pay-off deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the result or outcome, the eventual pay-off of something.

clue.text: Animal act takes time with Manx cat

indicators.note: takes means the word for act holds the time letter inside it

parts.note: play means act, as on stage

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its final letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A performance in which a tailless Isle of Man cat appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' signals a container and 'Manx' a docked tail: the Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, is famously tailless.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is an Australian egg-laying mammal, an example of an animal.

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
rust is the decay of iron

explanation.surface: A hospital ward is accused of falling into disrepair.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to entrust it to them; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tipping hat, single man is assiduous

indicators.note: tipping a hat tilts it over, so the word for hat is read backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A polite gentleman tipping his hat is a model of diligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipping' turns LID into DIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent and assiduous are synonyms: both describe careful, persevering work.

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: Old Nick, the Devil, has some connection with bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' reads as a name for the Devil; split it into O and a slang verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is the anatomical adjective for things of or concerning the skeleton.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people worry they have a chest infection.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that an ear infection is only one cause of the pain, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in the ear is commonly caused by an infection, so this is a loose, example-based definition.

parts.note: to enter is to record, as in a ledger

indicators.note: restricting means the word for contagion closes around the word for people

parts.note: taint is a contaminating influence, a contagion
men means people; the possessive is surface dressing

explanation.surface: Recording an outbreak of disease puts a stop to everyone's fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' is the container signal: the contagion word closes around the people. The 's on 'people's' is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment is amusement or enjoyment, a straightforward synonym of fun.

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Asking whether the retina is the source of a problem, and agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles RETINA and YES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes are a common problem, so this is a definition by category.

indicators.note: in means the word for stand goes inside the word for pubs

parts.note: bars are pubs
a rack is a stand, as for plates or bottles

explanation.surface: A drinker standing in pubs hurls abuse at others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a rack.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer or heckle, as a crowd does at a sporting event.

clue.text: In the main it's a bad drug

indicators.note: bad means these letters are spoiled into a different order

explanation.surface: On the whole, this drug is a harmful one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' shuffles the thirteen letters of IN THE MAIN ITS A.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihistamine is a medicine taken for allergies, so it is a kind of drug.

clue.text: Woman with eyes on family jewels?

definitions.text: Woman with eyes on family jewels?

parts.words: Woman with eyes on family jewels?
parts.note: a daughter set to inherit is eyeing up the family treasures she will one day own

explanation.surface: A covetous woman eyeing the family's heirlooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A female inheritor stands to receive the family's valuables when she succeeds.

clue.text: Copy of i consumed around Cambridge University

indicators.note: around means the first pieces wrap themselves about the university

parts.note: ate means consumed
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A copy of the i newspaper devoured around a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge University' suggests England, but it is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The i is a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy or mimic.

definitions.meaning: to put money into a venture in hope of profit is a kind of gamble
read as two words, a man without his shirt is down to his singlet

explanation.surface: A gambler who has lost everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost one's shirt' is the idiom for losing all one's money, but literally a shirtless man is IN VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Investing money carries risk, so it is a kind of gamble.

clue.text: Religious leader beginning to talk and talk

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader

indicators.note: beginning to says only the opening letter of the word that follows is wanted

explanation.surface: A rabbi starts a conversation and then just keeps on talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'talk' gives its initial letter; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length.

clue.text: Having a position when in sack

indicators.note: in means the word for when goes inside the word for sack

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone holds a post only while in the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being based somewhere means being stationed or located there.

clue.text: Baptise in church? Started holding tot's head

indicators.note: holding means the word for started keeps a letter inside it

parts.note: risen means started up, got going

indicators.note: head points to the opening letter of the word for a small child

explanation.surface: At a church baptism, someone lifts the infant's head as things begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts T, the head of 'tot's', inside RISEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To christen a child is to baptise it and give it a name in church.

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a standard abbreviation for the Queen
if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: The Queen supplied a growing ardour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ERIF upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is a figure for ardour and intense feeling.

indicators.note: found in means the alien's letters sit inside the word for immense

parts.note: cosmic means vast or immense
ET is the film's extraterrestrial, a stock crossword alien

explanation.surface: An alien being is discovered on a vast planetary surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surface' is the adjective sense: superficial, skin-deep.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic change is merely superficial, affecting only the outward look.

parts.note: Nice is the French city, so a woman there is addressed with the French courtesy title

explanation.surface: A pleasant lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like 'pleasant', but capitalised it is the city on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a married woman, used for a woman in a French city.

clue.text: Avoid sun at first, despite shivering

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it
shivering suggests trembling, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shuns the sunshine even though they are cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' is the anagram signal, making IDESTEP; 'despite' looks like a link word but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to dodge or evade it, an idiom for avoid.

clue.text: Pod exposed after nosing under topsoil initially

definitions.text: Pod exposed after nosing under topsoil initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: A seed pod is uncovered after rooting about beneath the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: this legume's pods ripen underground and are dug up.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut develops its pods below the soil, so they are exposed only by digging.
